newsitem.title: UK: Ldn precious metals retreat, led by shaky palladium.
newsitem.headline: Ldn precious metals retreat, led by shaky palladium.

text.p: The price of palladium gyrated on Friday as traders repositioned themselves against a a new twist in the fate of delayed Russian exports to Japan.
The rare white metal blipped up earlier, testing chart resistance at around $160.00 an ounce as traders began to doubt whether leading exporter Russia would resume shipments soon.
The price had dropped $5 on Thursday on news that a Moscow official said that a decree that should enable sales to start to Japan, the biggest importer, would be signed next week.
"We saw buying from several sources. London dealers, Swiss banks.A big order could have moved it this much," said a dealer.
But the price then eased back in tandem with New York, where the precious metals complex came under pressure from worse-than-expected U.S. inflation which pushed up T-bill and bond yields.
The March Producer Price Index (PPI) fell 0.1 percent from forecasts of unchanged, helping the strong dollar stay firm.
Gold was fixed lower at $347.95 an ounce from $348.65 after prices edged below $348 in rangebound dealings. But there was no sign of it breaking out of its cosy range as some had signalled.
Gold's upside was seen limited for now with physical demand satisfied at the current price levels. But even so, it could hold around $347.00 for the time being, one analyst said.
That view contradicted other forecasts that bullion's ability to stay above $345.00 could be tested again soon.
Palladium, mainly used in electronics and autocatalysts, was borrowed heavily in Europe, pushing the one-month lease rates back up to double-digit figures from about nine percent.
"The tightness is still there," said one dealer, adding that liquidation by some long holders had exacerbated a squeeze as less of that metal was now available for short-term lease.
Palladium pared gains in the afternoon as it stood just 25 cents up on the day at $156.00/157.00 an ounce at 1500 GMT.
Even so wild fluctuations were expected to continue until there was final proof that Russian exports would resume.
"Then it could fall dramatically in a major downward move and I would not be surprised to see $130-$140," one technical analyst said.
Its sister metal platinum spiked $3.50 up to $372.50 on Friday, a move analysts said was justified by constructive charts and a healthy physical demand scenario.
But it also retreated in the afternoon to stand at $371.25/$372.25, still up $2.25 on the day.
Silver was firm but off highs at $4.78/$4.80 with little options-related activity expected as open interest was clustered above $5.00. -- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
